title: Education
description: School uniforms and the week before an examination: the words of the two lessons (a uniform, to conform to a rule, to distinguish one group from another, smart in the sense of tidy and well dressed, to suppress, individuality, to cope with, to check, to fail, and a mind that goes blank) and the collocations they are locked into; the reflexive pronouns, whose table the book prints almost empty - myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, oneself, ourselves, yourselves, themselves - the two reasons for using one, the obligatory reflexive that fills the object place when the doer and the receiver are the same person (she blamed herself, they behaved themselves) and the emphatic reflexive that can be removed without touching the meaning (the pupils painted the room themselves); by plus a reflexive for an action done without help; the difference between each other, where two people act on one another, and themselves, where each one acts on himself; the verbs that take a reflexive in your own language and none at all in English (to feel, to relax, to concentrate, to hurry, to wake up, to meet); the modals of advice that the book practises without ever stating - should and ought to for advice and duty, had better and its negative had better not for the urgent warning, needn't for what is simply not necessary - each with the form of the verb that follows it; should have and shouldn't have plus the past participle for the duty that was not done, a reproach when it is addressed to somebody else and a regret when it is turned on oneself; expressing an opinion, agreeing and disagreeing, and expressing fear and worry before an examination; reading a school notice and telling what is forbidden from what is only advised and from what is merely unnecessary; and weighing the arguments for and against a school rule, including the concession a fair writer makes to the other side
sources: Official programme transcript - .claude/skills/content-ecole-tn/references/programmes-officiels/programme/2eme-sec/anglais.md, section 4 bis "Chapitre 07 - 07-education" (Theme VII, lessons 18-19, p. 100-107), section 2 "Book Map", Theme VII (Functions / Grammar / Vocabulary of L18 and L19), and the Appendix: Grammar summary "Lesson eighteen - Reflexive pronouns" (p. 172) and "Lesson nineteen - Modals" (p. 172-173), plus the lesson word lists (p. 180)
